title: patterns-data
description: The `data` payload of `dmtool patterns`, whose three routes return three different shapes. Which one you get is decided by the arguments, not by a flag: no argument lists the catalogue, an id alone describes that one idiom, and an id plus `--arg` scaffolds the artifact. A kernel-REJECTED scaffold returns the SAME shape as an accepted one — the scaffold is still reported so the author can see what was built and why it was refused; the verdict rides the envelope's `valid` (false) and `diagnostics`, not the payload. `--apply` is a different route entirely: it persists through `rule add`/`computation add`/`field add` and returns an `applied` envelope with `changed` and no `data`, so it is out of this schema's scope.

oneOf.title: catalogue
oneOf.description: `patterns` with no argument — every idiom, each with the `kind` of artifact it scaffolds.

count.description: How many idioms the catalogue holds.

id.description: The idiom id to pass back as `patterns <id>`.

summary.description: One line: what the idiom is for.

oneOf.title: idiom
oneOf.description: `patterns <id>` — one idiom in full, enough to compose the `--arg` list without guessing.

summary.description: One line: what the idiom is for.

skeleton.description: The artifact the idiom produces, with `<param>` placeholders left unsubstituted.

example.description: A ready-made argument set: parameter name → a sample value of the right kind. Pass each entry as one `--arg <name>=<value>` to get a working scaffold on the spot, rather than composing the values from `params[].kind` by hand.

polarityNote.description: Present on the rule idioms, absent on the others: a rule condition is TRUE on the VIOLATION, so this states which state the scaffolded condition describes. Read it before adapting the condition by hand — inverting it is the single most common authoring error the idioms exist to prevent.

oneOf.title: scaffold
oneOf.description: `patterns <id> --arg k=v …` — the artifact built from the idiom and auto-checked against the kernel. Returned whether the kernel accepted it or refused it; read the envelope's `valid` for the verdict.

pattern.description: The idiom id this was scaffolded from.

spec.description: The scaffolded artifact, in EXACTLY the shape the corresponding `add` verb consumes — so it can be piped straight into `rule add` / `computation add` / `field add`, which is what `--apply` does internally. The shape is `$ref`'d from those verbs' own input schemas rather than restated here: a restatement is invisible to every guard (it is well-formed JSON that conforms to its meta-schema and that no example executes), and this project has already shipped one that taught a form the tool refuses.

kind.description: Which artifact the idiom scaffolds, and therefore which `add` verb consumes its `spec`. `field` idioms are the field-level ALTERNATIVE to a rule — a bound or a pattern on the field itself, checked by the kernel without a rule at all.

paramNames.description: The parameter NAMES only, in skeleton order — the catalogue's lean projection. The detail route uses the separate `params` key for its object-valued parameter descriptions.

items.description: A parameter name; pass it as `--arg <name>=<value>`.

params.description: The idiom's parameters in full, in the order the skeleton reads them. Each is passed as one `--arg <name>=<value>`.

kind.description: What the value must be: a model path of a given field type (e.g. `number_field`, `date_field`), a bare `value` literal, or a group path. The idiom pre-flights it and refuses on stderr at exit 2 before any kernel call — so a wrong-typed argument is a usage error, never a scaffolded artifact.

doc.description: What this parameter means in the idiom.
